title: Latency bucketing, fallback routing and OTLP heuristics for per-request inference KPIs
creator: Monica Reyes
description:
Goal: Reduce high-cardinality noise and cost in the inference metrics pipeline while preserving accurate per-request KPIs (p50/p95/p99 and error rates) for SLO computation. This ticket implements three coordinated changes: (1) latency bucketing at the exporter/ingest edge to convert free-form latencies into fixed histogram buckets (reduces cardinality for downstream storage and avoids tail noise), (2) fallback routing that redirects heavy tenants/traffic spikes to a lower-resolution aggregator when capacity limits are reached, and (3) OTLP heuristic layer that applies deterministic sampling and label normalization for inference-specific keys (model, route, quantization_profile).

Workstreams & design decisions:
- Edge bucketing: Implement histogram bucketing in the lightweight sidecar (nodejs/golang) before OTLP export. Use exponential bucket boundaries tuned for tokenized request durations (10us -> 10s) with tighter buckets around typical response latencies (1ms - 2s). Trade-off: bucketing sacrifices per-request micro-precision but yields stable percentiles in Prometheus-compatible histograms and reduces label cardinality.
- Deterministic sampling heuristics: Use tenant-aware reservoir sampling keyed by (tenant_id, model_family) with rate overrides from config. This ensures reproducible samples for evaluations. Heuristics live in telemetry-config service with dynamic flags for emergency increases/decreases.
- Fallback routing: Introduce an OTLP router that directs telemetry to either (A) high-resolution pipeline (influx/otel-collector -> prometheus-exposer) or (B) low-resolution rollup store when tenant throughput exceeds a sliding-window threshold. Low-res path writes summarized histograms and aggregate counters only.
- Label normalization: Strip high-cardinality labels (user_id, session_id) and standardize model variant tags (e.g., gptx-13b -> model_family:gptx, model_size:13b). Add an optional tag quantization_profile for downstream quality-cost analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- Endpoint-level p50/p95/p99 produced from histogram buckets match current high-resolution metrics within +/- 5% on control traffic.
- Prometheus cardinality observed per-tenant drops by >= 40% in canary tenants.
- No increase in error budget burn for production routes during canary and staged rollout.
- Canary shows expected cost reduction (estimated 18-25% ingestion egress savings) and SLOs preserved.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike & benchmarks (complete) — microbench sidecar CPU/memory and serialization overhead.
2) Implement bucketing + normalization in sidecar (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1425).
3) Build OTLP router with promotion/fallback logic (branch: telemetry/otlp-router-fallback).
4) Create feature flags and config schema in telemetry-config service (dashboard + api to adjust sampling rates).
5) Canary: roll to 5% of tenants (low-risk tenants identified by product) for 48 hours, monitor latency percentiles, ingestion rate, and cardinality.
6) If canary passes, staged ramp to 50% then 100% over 2 weeks.

Testing & monitoring:
- Unit + integration tests for bucket boundaries and histogram aggregation.
- Load test using synthetic workload generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/loadbench, scenario: inference-100k-rps-short) to validate cost and correctness at scale.
- Dashboards to observe: ingestion rate, per-tenant unique label cardinality, histogram-derived percentiles vs. ground truth traces, error budget burn, sidecar CPU/RAM.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bucketing could distort percentile calculation for extremely low-latency services. Mitigation: allow per-route opt-out and tighter buckets via flag.
- Risk: Router misclassification could drop critical telemetry. Mitigation: dual-write mode during rollout (write to both high-res and rollup stores for a sampling window) and reconciliation jobs.
- Risk: Unexpected increase in sidecar resource usage. Mitigation: benchmarked limits and canary resource throttle.

Dependencies:
- telemetry-config service schema update (PR link above).
- Console dashboard update to visualize histogram percentile derivation and cardinality (PM: link to design doc below).
